frequency_question: How often have states successfully stood up domestic production of high-tech missiles under active wartime constraints within a two-year window?
membership_rule: Includes state-backed efforts to transition from receiving foreign advanced cruise/ballistic missiles to domestic assembly or manufacture under active conflict; excludes routine peacetime technology transfers or low-tech munitions like artillery shells.

cases.name: Nazi Germany V-2 production relocation to Mittelwerk
Taiwan Hsiung Feng missile program localization
Iran domestic anti-ship missile production (derived from Chinese/North Korean blueprints)

provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 3 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 3 named; represents the exhaustive set of high-complexity state-level missile localization under acute duress.
known_gaps: Modern software-defined guidance systems and Western supply chain security protocols represent a higher friction barrier than 20th-century reverse engineering.
skeleton: 3 historical episodes of wartime/embargoed advanced missile localization, yielding 3 hits.
multiplier: 3/3 cases successful under high duress, but modern cruise missile subsystems involve microchips and complex supply chains absent in historical analogues.
validity_reason: Geopolitical and industrial localization dynamics change slowly over decades.
